title: Young bands and a ladies' brass band
summary: Organising a twenty-piece young band and a women's brass band that would not practice.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Just losing time, see. Did you ever work with a whole band, a young band, to try to teach the whole band together?

Yeah, I had a young band, yeah. I had them put them. I had, oh, twenty some odd pieces. I had them together and I put them together. Sometimes I'd take them out of the first grade on the band and all the good ones, I pick them out. The baritone, you're clarinet, you can play in three sharps, two sharps. If a man can play in two sharps, you can take them, you can put them in the band. He'll make out, see. Two sharps or two flats, you can put them in there, he'll make out, see. Then you get them little low grade ones, first grade ones. The boys, they didn't know the instruments, they just know the scales, you know. Well, I wouldn't put them, I wouldn't tell them later on that they'd learn how to play, you know, on a different scale. Then I let them in. Oh, I had a ton. Good band, some halfway bands, some of them wasn't going to like nothing because they, I had a band of, I had a band of ladies. They were good. Really? But the, but the teacher up there, yeah. Well, there's a picture up there. Yeah. Is that the one? Yeah, that's one. That's it, yeah. But that's some of the women, but I wasn't in that, this is another fellow got this, but there's some of the women in there. Oh, some of that. And, uh. Sorry, the brass band? Yeah, it was a brass band. And, uh, I don't know. They was playing and practicing and playing. They could play a number. When I picked them up, see, they was playing already. But there wasn't one of them women who hardly could play a scale. Couldn't play a scale. Played by ear and? Played by, well, they knew the notes, but they, I don't know what, you know, I don't know what you could say about them.
They wouldn't practice that, I guess.

I guess they needed to practice, see, and study. And, uh, they wouldn't study. And whenever they had a job, yeah, women would come out of their homes, man, full of cobweb. They done had it hanging up. Before I forget. But they hear about a job. When they hear about a job, there's those women that's playing. Sure, they got homes, you know, even shine them up. You know how it felt. Yeah.
